\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Hermite affine integral recurrence]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_hermite_affine_recurrence}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_hermite_affine_recurrence}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.derivative_hermite_succ, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_polynomial_mul_affine_standardGaussian, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_id_mul_polynomial_affine_standardGaussian, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $k$ be a natural number and let $\rho,s,x\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $\rho^2+s^2=1$. The
standard Gaussian integral of the Hermite polynomial of degree $k+2$ evaluated at $\rho
x+s y$ equals $\rho x$ times the corresponding integral for degree $k+1$, minus
$(k+1)\rho^2$ times the corresponding integral for degree $k$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Hermite polynomial under Gaussian affine averaging]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_hermite_affine_standardGaussian}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_hermite_affine_standardGaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.derivative_hermite_succ, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_hermite_affine_recurrence, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k$ be a natural number and let $\rho,s,x\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $\rho^2+s^2=1$. The
standard Gaussian integral of the Hermite polynomial of degree $k$ evaluated at $\rho
x+s y$ equals $\rho^k$ times the Hermite polynomial of degree $k$ evaluated at $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Affine Averaging of Normalized Hermite Polynomials]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_normalizedHermite_affine_standardGaussian}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_normalizedHermite_affine_standardGaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_hermite_affine_standardGaussian, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $k$ and real numbers $\rho,s,x$ satisfying $\rho^2+s^2=1$, the
normalized Hermite polynomial $H_k$ obeys
\[
\int_{\mathbb R} H_k(\rho x+sy)\,d\gamma(y)=\rho^k H_k(x),
\]
where $\gamma$ is the standard Gaussian probability measure.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)\in\mathbb N^n$, and
let $\rho\in[-1,1]$. For the multivariate normalized Hermite function $H_\alpha$ on
$\mathbb R^n$, Gaussian noise of correlation $\rho$ acts by
\[T_\rho H_\alpha=\rho^{\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_n}H_\alpha.\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Correlated Hermite moment]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermite_correlated_moment}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermite_correlated_moment}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_hermiteFunction, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction_memLp_two, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_correlatedGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_hermiteFunction_mul}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\boldsymbol{\beta},\boldsymbol{\beta}'\in\bbn^n$, and let
$\rho\in[-1,1]$. If $(X,Y)$ has the law obtained by taking independent standard Gaussian
vectors $Z,W\in\bbr^n$ and setting $X=Z$ and $Y=\rho Z+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}W$, then
\[
\mathbb{E}\bigl[H_{\boldsymbol{\beta}}(X)H_{\boldsymbol{\beta}'}(Y)\bigr]=
\begin{cases}
\rho^{|\boldsymbol{\beta}|},&\boldsymbol{\beta}=\boldsymbol{\beta}',\\
0,&\boldsymbol{\beta}\ne\boldsymbol{\beta}',
\end{cases}
\]
where $H_{\boldsymbol{\beta}}$ denotes the multivariate normalized Hermite function and
$|\boldsymbol{\beta}|=\sum_{i=1}^n\beta_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Hermite coefficients under Gaussian noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_gaussianNoise}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_gaussianNoise}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_hermiteFunction, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_selfAdjoint, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction_memLp_two}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be square-integrable with
respect to the $n$-dimensional standard Gaussian measure, and let $\rho\in[-1,1]$. For
every multi-index $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$, the Hermite coefficient of the Gaussian-noise
smoothing of $f$ at $\alpha$ equals $\rho^{|\alpha|}$ times the Hermite coefficient of
$f$ at $\alpha$, where $|\alpha|=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i$.
\end{theorem}
